rationale: POST /auth/forgot-password answers { success, message } with no error envelope and no code, so there is nothing on the wire for the resolver to classify. Migrating as-is would replace the server's reason with "check your input" on every 400. The endpoint has to emit a code first.

GET /auth/reset-password/verify answers { valid, ... } with no code. A spent reset link and a malformed one are both 400, and the shared 400 copy tells the reader to check their input, which is not something they typed.
POST /auth/reset-password answers { success, message } with no code, so a weak password and an expired token are indistinguishable to the client. Same prerequisite as the other two.

The global handler builds its own Error from window 'error' and 'unhandledrejection' events, so this message is JavaScript's, not a server response. The only consumer today passes showToast:false, so it does not reach a toast at all.

Reports a shortcut handler throwing -- a browser-side error with no HTTP response to classify. The composable has no translator, so routing it through the resolver would trade a real message for "an unknown error occurred".
Reports a shortcuts JSON import failing -- a parse error on a file the user just picked, so the parser's own message is the useful part and there is no response to classify.
Kept deliberately alongside code and status: LoginView translates from those two, and this string is what the store's console.error prints. Removing it would make a lockout undiagnosable from a log.
Token refresh runs in the background; its failure logs out or retries rather than rendering. Nothing displays this field.

code: const message = getApiErrorMessage(error, "Token 驗證失敗");
rationale: Token validation runs on boot and its failure redirects to login rather than rendering a message.

code: const message = getApiErrorMessage(error, "獲取用戶資訊失敗");
rationale: Profile fetch failure is handled by the caller's own state, not by displaying this string.

code: const message = getApiErrorMessage(error, "獲取訂單失敗");
rationale: The orders store rethrows this as a bare Error, so the resolver sees no code or status and answers with the generic copy. Nothing leaks -- the resolver ignores message -- but every kitchen API failure reads the same. Fixing it means carrying code and status the way authApi now does.

code: const message = getApiErrorMessage(error, "更新狀態失敗");
rationale: Same as the orders fetch above: the message survives only into the log, and the classification that would tell a chef whether the item was already served is lost on the way.
Recorded on the queued action for retry bookkeeping and the error-report dashboard. No template renders OfflineAction.error.
The replay result is consumed by the sync loop to decide whether to retry, not by a view.
